newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises 70 bps to 11.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises 70 bps to 11.5 pct.

text.p: Strong demand and weaker supply pushed the Croatian average lending rate up 70 basis points to 11.5 percent on Friday.
The day's trade totalled 39.1 million kuna, as banks could not meet demand amounting to 45 million. More than half the trade was call money that remained stable at 10.5 percent.
All but 8.8 million kuna of the turnover were fresh loans.

Insurers rolled over their old one-week loans at nine percent. Banks charged 13 and 15 percent for renewed two-week loans and 15 percent for one-month money with the exception of one sum borrowed by a savings bank at 17 percent.

The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Saturday slightly stronger at 6.1435 against the dollar and a little weaker at 3.5774 against the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom 385 1 4557075
